syllabusTopics: Protista: Outline classification. Protozoa: diagnostic features and classification up to class with examples
Paramecium caudatum, Plasmodium vivax: habits and habitat, structure, reproduction, life-cycle
Animalia: Level of organization, body plan, body symmetry, body cavity and segmentation in animals

Diagnostic features and classification of phyla (up to class): Porifera, Coelenterata (Cnidaria), Platyhelminthes, Aschelminthes (Nemathelminthes), Annelida, Arthropoda, Mollusca, Echinodermata and Chordata
Earthworm (Pheretima posthuma): Habit and habitat, external features; digestive system (alimentary canal and physiology of digestion)
Earthworm: Excretory system (types of nephridia, structure and arrangement of septal nephridia); nervous system (central and peripheral, working mechanism)
Earthworm: Reproductive systems (male and female reproductive organs), copulation, cocoon formation and economic importance
Frog (Rana tigrina): Habit and habitat, external features; digestive system (alimentary canal, digestive glands and physiology of digestion)
Frog: Blood vascular system (structure and working mechanism of heart); respiratory system (respiratory organs and physiology of respiration)
Frog: Reproductive system (male and female reproductive organs)

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Protozoa are animal-like, mostly unicellular eukaryotes classified by their locomotion into four classes: Sarcodina (pseudopodia, e.g. Amoeba), Mastigophora (flagella, e.g. Trypanosoma), Ciliophora (cilia, e.g. Paramecium), and Sporozoa (non-motile spores, e.g. Plasmodium). Paramecium and Amoeba are model organisms. Plasmodium (malaria) with its Anopheles vector is a key NEB examination topic.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Protozoa classes: Sarcodina (pseudopodia), Mastigophora (flagella), Ciliophora (cilia), Sporozoa (spores/non-motile)
Amoeba: cell membrane + cytoplasm + nucleus + food vacuole + contractile vacuole
Paramecium: cilia + oral groove + food vacuole + macro/micronucleus + contractile vacuole

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Protists are eukaryotes (have a nucleus); they are NOT bacteria (prokaryotes).  ·  Protozoa are animal-like; algae are plant-like; slime moulds are fungus-like — all are in Protista.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects a labelled Paramecium diagram and the 4-class Protozoa table.  ·  Plasmodium life cycle (human + mosquito) with Anopheles vector is a very frequent long-answer.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Amoeba proteus — Sarcodina; pseudopodia; no fixed shape.  ·  Paramecium caudatum — Ciliophora; cilia; two nuclei; oral groove.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Amoeba moves by pseudopodia (no flagella/cilia); Paramecium by cilia; Trypanosoma by flagella.  ·  Sporozoa (Plasmodium) are non-motile in their adult/infective (spore) stage; they do not have flagella/cilia/pseudopodia.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Tabulate 4 Protozoa classes  ·  Label Paramecium

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Protozoa = Proto (first) + zoon (animal).  ·  Amoeba = pseudo (false foot) = pseudopodia.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Why is Protista called a "kingdom of convenience"?  ·  Classify Protozoa up to class with diagnostic features.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Draw and label Paramecium — very common.  ·  Tabulate the 4 Protozoa classes (locomotion, example, disease).

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Protozoa classification (4 classes)  ·  Pseudopodia/cilia/flagella  ·  Amoeba structure  ·  Paramecium (two nuclei, oral groove)

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Protista: eukaryotic, mostly unicellular; animal/plant/fungus-like.  ·  Protozoa = animal-like; locomotion defines the 4 classes.  ·  Sarcodina (Amoeba) — pseudopodia; Ciliophora (Paramecium) — cilia.  ·  Mastigophora (Trypanosoma) — flagella; Sporozoa (Plasmodium) — non-motile spores.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Amoeba proteus is ~0.5 mm; Paramecium is ~0.2 mm long.  ·  Plasmodium falciparum causes the most deadly form of malaria (P. vivax, P. malariae, P. ovale are others).

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: Explain the structure and locomotion of Paramecium.  ·  Describe the life cycle of Plasmodium with the role of Anopheles.  ·  Differentiate the four protozoan classes.

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: Explain the Plasmodium life cycle with Anopheles.  ·  Differentiate Amoeba from Paramecium.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Trypanosoma brucei — Mastigophora; flagellum; causes sleeping sickness.  ·  Plasmodium falciparum — Sporozoa; no locomotion; causes malaria; Anopheles vector.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: Paramecium moves by: → B  ·  The malaria-causing protozoan is: → C

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Protista: eukaryotic, mostly unicellular (some colonial); the "kingdom of convenience" for single-celled eukaryotes.  ·  Protozoa (animal-like protists): heterotrophic, motile; grouped by locomotion — Sarcodina (Amoeba, pseudopodia), Mastigophora (Trypanosoma, flagella), Ciliophora (Paramecium, cilia), Sporozoa (Plasmodium, non-motile spores).  ·  Amoeba proteus: pseudopodia for movement + food; contractile vacuole; no definite shape.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Plasmodium life cycle  ·  Anopheles vector  ·  Osmoregulation

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Paramecium has two nuclei (macro + micro) and contractile vacuoles.  ·  Plasmodium: malaria; Anopheles vector; human + mosquito life cycle.  ·  Paramecium has TWO nuclei: a large macro-nucleus (metabolic) and a small micro-nucleus (reproductive).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Contractile vacuole in freshwater protozoa expels excess water (osmoregulation); it is not a "digestive" vacuole.  ·  Amoeba pseudopodia vs Paramecium cilia — a common differentiation.  ·  Paramecium's two nuclei (macro + micro) is a distinctive exam point.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Memorise the 4 Protozoa classes (locomotion + example).  ·  Draw and label Paramecium and Amoeba.  ·  Learn the Plasmodium life cycle (human + mosquito).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Note the role of Anopheles in malaria transmission.  ·  Explain osmoregulation via the contractile vacuole.  ·  Protozoa are animal-like protists that move by pseudopodia, flagella, or cilia.
